title: Significant cardiac disease
protocolCondition: Heart conditions: angina, chest pain, heart failure, irregular heartbeat, heart attack, or narrowing of a heart valve
summary: Reject. BNF contraindicates significant cardiac disease for dapoxetine.
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 — BNF contraindication: “significant cardiac disease”
rationale: This list operationalises what the BNF’s “significant cardiac disease” contraindication covers in practice; dapoxetine also carries its own cardiovascular caution profile (hypotension, syncope, rare arrhythmia). Decline and signpost to GP.
rejectIf: Angina, chest pain, heart failure, irregular heartbeat, heart attack, or valvular narrowing on history/SCR
Any disclosure that maps to significant cardiac disease

title: Low blood pressure and orthostatic intolerance
matchRuleNames: Low blood pressure and orthostatic intolerance
protocolRef: S5 — Low blood pressure (below 90/50) or tendency to faint on standing
protocolCondition: Low blood pressure (below 90/50) or a tendency to faint or feel light-headed on standing
summary: Reject. Postural hypotension / orthostatic intolerance — remote pathway cannot perform the SmPC orthostatic test.
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 — BNF contraindications: “postural hypotension”, “history of syncope”; SmPC pre-treatment screening calls for a formal orthostatic test
rationale: Postural hypotension and history of syncope are named BNF contraindications. The SmPC’s recommended safeguard — an in-person supine/standing blood pressure and pulse test before first prescribing — cannot be performed remotely (Section 1), so this service relies on self-reported history and declines rather than proceeding on an unverified answer.
rejectIf: Tendency to faint or feel light-headed on standing
searchTags: drop in blood pressure on standing

title: Recurrent or unexplained syncope
protocolCondition: Recurrent fainting (Syncope)
summary: Reject. Recurrent or unexplained syncope is a named BNF contraindication.
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 — BNF contraindication: “history of syncope”
rationale: Directly matches a named BNF contraindication; duplicated deliberately alongside the low blood pressure/light-headedness question for clarity. SCR wording suggesting recurrent, unexplained, or cardiac syncope blocks supply.
rejectIf: History of syncope without a clear benign trigger

title: Isolated vasovagal syncope with identified trigger
matchRuleNames: Isolated vasovagal syncope with identified trigger
protocolRef: S5 / S9 — Flagged tier of the two-tier syncope rule
protocolCondition: Isolated vasovagal syncope with identified trigger (flagged tier)
summary: Flag for prescriber review. Isolated triggered vasovagal syncope is the softer tier of the two-tier syncope rule.
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 / S9 — BNF “history of syncope” — two-tier SCR rule; S9 framework not algorithm
rationale: Recurrent/unexplained syncope rejects. A single, clearly triggered vasovagal episode may be judged within the protocol’s framework rather than automatic decline — record reasoning. Escalate to reject if recurrent keywords also match.
askPatient: Was this a single vasovagal episode with a clear trigger?

title: Treated hypertension
protocolCondition: Medicines that lower blood pressure or cause vasodilation / treated hypertension
summary: Reject. Treated hypertension implies BP-lowering medicines that add to dapoxetine’s orthostatic risk.
source: EDM-PE-01 S7 — S7 blood-pressure-lowering medicines — SERVICE-LEVEL POLICY
rationale: Dapoxetine causes dose-related postural hypotension and syncope (Section 6). Any medicine that independently lowers blood pressure is additive. This service cannot perform the SmPC’s recommended supine-and-standing BP test, so it declines rather than counselling.

title: Recorded blood pressure value
protocolCondition: Low blood pressure (below 90/50)
summary: Reject when recorded BP is below 90/50 (or equivalent low reading triggering the numeric rule).
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 — BNF postural hypotension / SmPC orthostatic screening gap
rationale: Named BNF contraindication territory. Remote service cannot verify orthostatic reserve with the SmPC’s recommended in-person test, so low recorded BP blocks supply.
rejectIf: Systolic < 90 or diastolic < 50 on SCR reading matching the PE numeric rule

title: Recorded postural blood pressure assessment
protocolCondition: Recorded postural blood pressure assessment (orthostatic screening gap)
summary: Flag. Postural BP text on SCR highlights the orthostatic screening gap — review before supply.
source: EDM-PE-01 S1 / S12 — Section 1 / 12 — inability to perform SmPC orthostatic test is the largest known pathway gap
rationale: Inability to perform the SmPC’s recommended in-person orthostatic test is the single largest known gap between this protocol and intended safe use (Section 12). A recorded postural assessment should prompt careful review of values and symptoms.
askPatient: Confirm latest lying/standing BP and symptoms on standing

title: Psychiatric contraindications
protocolRef: S5 — Severe depression, mania, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia
protocolCondition: History of depression (severe), mania, bipolar disorder, or schizophrenia
summary: Reject. Severe depression, mania, bipolar disorder, or schizophrenia (service policy).
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 — BNF contraindications for severe depression / mania / bipolar; schizophrenia SERVICE-LEVEL POLICY
rationale: Severe depression, mania and bipolar disorder are named BNF contraindications. Schizophrenia is not itself named in the BNF list for dapoxetine, but this service declines it as a precaution given the serotonergic/psychiatric-symptom profile and interaction risk with antipsychotics such as thioridazine (Section 7).

title: Self-harm and suicidality
protocolRef: S5 — Severe depression; S6 — psychiatric adverse effects
protocolCondition: Self-harm / suicidality (psychiatric safety)
summary: Reject. Self-harm or suicidality signals block remote dapoxetine supply.
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 / S6 — S5 severe depression; S6 — discontinue if psychiatric disorder develops; S8 / S11 safety-netting
rationale: Aligned with severe-depression contraindication and counselling that mood changes or thoughts of self-harm require stopping and seeking medical help immediately (Sections 6, 8, 11).
rejectIf: Active psychiatric crisis markers on SCR

title: Historical or non-severe depression
protocolCondition: Resolved single episode of non-severe depression (worked scenario 5)
summary: Flag for review. Resolved, non-severe historical depression is not an automatic reject under S9 scenario 5.
source: EDM-PE-01 S9 — BNF wording is “history of severe depression” — prescriber judgement; record reasoning
rationale: A 33-year-old with a single treated episode five years ago, fully resolved and not on antidepressants: under the BNF’s own wording the contraindication is specifically “history of severe depression”. Judgement whether a resolved non-severe episode meets that bar sits within this protocol’s framework; keep recorded reasoning (Section 1 — framework, not algorithm).

title: Epilepsy and seizure disorders
protocolCondition: Epilepsy
summary: Reject any epilepsy history — service cannot verify seizure control remotely.
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 — BNF: uncontrolled epilepsy contraindication; controlled epilepsy caution — SERVICE-LEVEL POLICY to decline all
rationale: The BNF only contraindicates uncontrolled epilepsy outright; controlled epilepsy is a caution (discontinue if convulsions develop). This service cannot verify seizure control remotely, so it declines any history of epilepsy rather than attempt that distinction.

title: Hepatic impairment
protocolRef: S5 — Moderate or severe liver problems
protocolCondition: Moderate or severe liver problems
summary: Reject. Moderate/severe hepatic impairment — disclosed liver problems declined because severity cannot be verified remotely.
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 — BNF: avoid in moderate to severe hepatic impairment
rationale: Direct BNF contraindication for moderate to severe hepatic impairment. Mild impairment is not addressed by that wording; disclosed liver problems of any stated severity are declined because severity cannot be verified remotely.

title: Renal impairment
protocolCondition: Kidney problems
summary: Reject. Any disclosed kidney problem — severity cannot be verified without a blood test this service does not routinely require.
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 — BNF: caution CrCl 30–80; avoid if under 30 — remote service declines any disclosed kidney problem
rationale: Renal impairment severity cannot be verified without a blood test this service does not routinely require. Any disclosed kidney problem is declined rather than risk unrecognised severe impairment, where dapoxetine should be avoided.
rejectIf: Kidney / renal disease on history or SCR

title: Recorded eGFR value
protocolCondition: Kidney problems (numeric eGFR)
summary: Reject when eGFR/CrCl on SCR triggers the PE renal numeric rule (severe impairment / unverified risk).
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 — BNF renal dosing — avoid if CrCl under 30; caution 30–80
rationale: BNF advises caution if creatinine clearance 30–80 mL/min and avoid if under 30. Numeric hits that indicate unsafe or unverifiable renal status block supply.

title: Glaucoma and raised intraocular pressure
protocolRef: S5 — History of glaucoma, raised IOP, or told at increased risk
protocolCondition: History of glaucoma, told you are at increased risk of glaucoma, or raised intraocular pressure
summary: Reject. Glaucoma / raised IOP / told at increased risk — eye examination cannot be provided remotely.
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 — BNF caution: susceptibility to angle-closure glaucoma — SERVICE-LEVEL POLICY to decline
rationale: The BNF lists this as a caution requiring clinical judgement, not an absolute contraindication. This service declines rather than proceeds, since angle-closure glaucoma risk needs an eye examination this pathway cannot provide. Family-history “at increased risk” remains reject (unlike other family-history downgrades).
rejectIf: Told at increased risk of glaucoma (including family history wording)

title: Topical glaucoma treatments
protocolCondition: Topical glaucoma treatments (corroborating signal)
summary: Reject. Glaucoma eye drops corroborate the S5 glaucoma / raised-IOP exclusion.
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 — S5 glaucoma exclusion — corroborating medication signal
rationale: Topical glaucoma treatments on the SCR support that the patient has glaucoma or raised IOP needing examination this pathway cannot provide — decline per Section 5 service policy.
rejectIf: Active topical glaucoma therapy on SCR

title: Bleeding and clotting disorders
protocolRef: S5 — History of bleeding or clotting problems
protocolCondition: History of bleeding or blood-clotting problems
summary: Reject. Bleeding/clotting disorders — remote pathway cannot grade severity.
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 — BNF caution: bleeding disorders — SERVICE-LEVEL POLICY to decline rather than caution
rationale: The BNF lists this as a caution, not an absolute contraindication, reflecting bleeding-risk interaction between serotonergic drugs and clotting. This service declines rather than proceeds with caution.

title: Prostate conditions
protocolCondition: Prostate problems
summary: Reject. Prostate problems — may mimic PE/urinary symptoms; tamsulosin interaction risk (S7).
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 — SERVICE-LEVEL POLICY — not a named BNF/SmPC contraindication for dapoxetine
rationale: Prostate disease is not itself listed as a dapoxetine contraindication. It is included because prostate conditions can cause or mimic ejaculatory and urinary symptoms that need proper assessment, and because tamsulosin (common BPH treatment) has a genuine additive hypotension interaction with dapoxetine (Section 7).
rejectIf: Prostate disease / BPH / prostate cancer markers on SCR

title: Genitourinary symptoms and infection
protocolRef: S5 — Pain on ejaculation, or difficulty/pain passing urine
protocolCondition: Pain whilst ejaculating, or difficulty or pain passing urine
summary: Reject. Dysuria or pain on ejaculation points away from straightforward PE and needs assessment first.
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 — EAU guidelines as summarised in NICE ESNM40
rationale: EAU guidelines state that a genitourinary infection (for example prostatitis) or other cause should be identified and treated first; dysuria or pain on ejaculation needs assessment this pathway cannot provide.

title: Erectile dysfunction
protocolRef: S5 — Erectile dysfunction, whether treated or untreated
protocolCondition: Difficulty getting or keeping an erection (erectile dysfunction), whether currently treated or untreated
summary: Reject. ED — treated or untreated — is excluded from this PE pathway.
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 — EAU (untreated ED); SERVICE-LEVEL POLICY for treated ED; SmPC PDE5 interaction
rationale: EAU guidance: erectile dysfunction should be identified and treated before premature ejaculation, because PE is frequently secondary to it. Treated ED is also excluded because PDE5 inhibitors are a named contraindication to dapoxetine on syncope grounds (Section 7) and cannot be co-prescribed.

title: Galactose intolerance and lactose-related disorders
protocolRef: S5 — Galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, glucose-galactose malabsorption
protocolCondition: Galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption
summary: Reject. Hereditary galactose/lactose-related disorders — tablet excipient contraindication.
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 — Standard excipient-based contraindication (lactose in film-coated tablets)
rationale: Standard safety wording for film-coated tablets that contain lactose as an excipient, consistent with other oral medicines in this class of consultation question.

title: Thyroid dysfunction
protocolCondition: Thyroid dysfunction (acquired PE indicator — proposed)
summary: Flag. Thyroid dysfunction may indicate acquired PE needing wider assessment.
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 — Proposed acquired-PE row — flag for prescriber review
rationale: Acquired PE can be secondary to endocrine or other medical causes. Thyroid dysfunction on SCR should prompt review that the licensed PE diagnosis and exclusion pathway still hold.

title: MAOIs and reversible MAO inhibitors
protocolCondition: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors (e.g. selegiline, moclobemide, phenelzine) and linezolid (a weak MAOI)
summary: Reject. MAOIs / linezolid — named contraindication; washout not managed remotely.
source: EDM-PE-01 S7 — SmPC (via ESNM40): named contraindicated class
rationale: Named contraindicated class. A washout period is typically required either side of MAOI use with any serotonergic drug; this service declines outright rather than attempt to manage timing remotely.

title: Antidepressants of all classes
protocolRef: S7 — SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs and other antidepressants
protocolCondition: SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs and other antidepressants
summary: Reject. Antidepressants of all classes — serotonin syndrome / named contraindications.
source: EDM-PE-01 S7 — SmPC (via ESNM40): concomitant SSRIs/TCAs contraindicated; SNRIs by class extension
rationale: Concomitant SSRIs are contraindicated because of additive serotonergic effects and risk of serotonin syndrome. SNRIs carry the same risk by class extension. TCAs are a named contraindicated class.
rejectIf: SSRI, SNRI, TCA or other antidepressant on SCR

title: Antipsychotics and lithium
protocolRef: S7 — Thioridazine and lithium (service extension to the class)
protocolCondition: Thioridazine and lithium (service extension to antipsychotics class)
summary: Reject. Thioridazine, lithium, and service extension to antipsychotics.
source: EDM-PE-01 S7 — SmPC names thioridazine; lithium linked to bipolar contraindication + serotonergic risk
rationale: SmPC names thioridazine specifically as contraindicated. Lithium is included because it is typically prescribed for bipolar disorder (itself a dapoxetine contraindication in Section 5) and carries recognised serotonergic-interaction risk with SSRIs generally. Service extends caution across antipsychotics listed in consultation Step 6.

title: Triptans
protocolCondition: Triptans (e.g. sumatriptan, rizatriptan, zolmitriptan)
summary: Reject. Triptans — recognised serotonin syndrome risk with SSRIs.
source: EDM-PE-01 S7 — Class-wide serotonin syndrome risk with SSRIs — precautionary reject
rationale: Recognised class-wide serotonin syndrome risk with SSRIs; not named specifically in the ESNM40 SmPC excerpt but a well-established interaction for this drug class, applied as a precaution. Cross-clinic note: EDM-MIG-01.

title: Other serotonergic agents
protocolRef: S7 — St John's Wort, L-tryptophan, tramadol
protocolCondition: St John's Wort, tryptophan, tramadol and other serotonergic agents
summary: Reject. St John’s Wort, L-tryptophan, tramadol and related serotonergic agents.
source: EDM-PE-01 S7 — SmPC herbal serotonergic products; tramadol serotonin + seizure-threshold risk
rationale: SmPC contraindicates herbal/medicinal products with serotonergic effects. Tramadol inhibits serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake, creating serotonin syndrome risk with any SSRI, and independently lowers seizure threshold — additive with dapoxetine’s SSRI-class effect.

title: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors
protocolCondition: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (macrolides, azoles, HIV protease inhibitors)
summary: Reject. Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors — genotype-dependent exception cannot be verified remotely.
source: EDM-PE-01 S7 — BNF: avoid potent CYP3A4 inhibitors unless verified extensive CYP2D6 metaboliser
rationale: BNF: avoid with concurrent use of potent inhibitors of CYP3A4, except in patients verified as extensive CYP2D6 metabolisers (where a 30 mg cap applies) — a distinction this service cannot verify remotely, so it declines outright.

title: Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors
protocolCondition: Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. some antifungals, nefazodone, verapamil, diltiazem)
summary: Reject. Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors — cannot verify CYP2D6 status for 30 mg-only pathway.
source: EDM-PE-01 S7 — BNF: max 30 mg with moderate inhibitors unless CYP2D6 status verified — service declines
rationale: Manufacturer advises a maximum 30 mg dose with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors unless CYP2D6 metaboliser status is verified. As this service cannot verify genotype, it declines rather than attempt a 30 mg-only pathway. Aprepitant is also treated under this CYP3A4 policy (Section 7).
rejectIf: Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor on SCR (e.g. verapamil, diltiazem, aprepitant)

title: Nitrates and nitric oxide donors
protocolCondition: Nitrates and nitric oxide donors / vasodilators
summary: Reject. Nitrates / NO donors add to dapoxetine’s postural hypotension and syncope risk.
source: EDM-PE-01 S7 — S7 BP-lowering and vasodilating medicines — SERVICE-LEVEL POLICY
rationale: Dapoxetine causes dose-related postural hypotension and syncope. Any medicine that independently lowers blood pressure or causes vasodilation is additive. Without the SmPC orthostatic test, the service declines.
rejectIf: Nitrate or nitric oxide donor therapy

title: Alpha-blockers
protocolCondition: Alpha-blockers for prostate symptoms or blood pressure (e.g. tamsulosin, doxazosin)
summary: Reject. Alpha-blockers — additive orthostatic hypotension with dapoxetine.
source: EDM-PE-01 S7 — Additive orthostatic hypotension risk with dapoxetine
rationale: Additive orthostatic hypotension risk with dapoxetine’s own postural hypotension profile (Section 6). Applies whether prescribed for prostate symptoms or for blood pressure.

title: Antihypertensives and rate-controlling medicines
protocolRef: S7 — Blood-pressure-lowering medicines; medicines affecting heart rate or rhythm
protocolCondition: Antihypertensives and medicines affecting heart rate or rhythm (e.g. digoxin, beta-blockers)
summary: Reject. Antihypertensives and rate/rhythm medicines — additive cardiac/hypotension risk.
source: EDM-PE-01 S7 — S7 BP-lowering / rate-control medicines — SERVICE-LEVEL POLICY
rationale: Not always specifically named in the SmPC excerpt, but a reasonable precaution given dapoxetine’s cardiac and hypotension cautions and that this service already declines significant cardiac disease (Section 5). Beta-blockers, digoxin and other antihypertensives are declined.

title: PDE5 inhibitors and other ED treatments
matchRuleNames: PDE5 inhibitors and other ED treatments
protocolCondition: Phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitors for erectile dysfunction
summary: Reject. PDE5 inhibitors — named contraindication (syncope / orthostatic tolerance).
source: EDM-PE-01 S7 — SmPC (via ESNM40): do not use with PDE5 inhibitors — increased syncope risk
rationale: Dapoxetine should not be used in men taking PDE5 inhibitors, as the combination increases the risk of syncope. Also reflects that dapoxetine is not a treatment for ED and should not be combined with ED medicines. Cross-clinic: EDM-ED-01.
rejectIf: Sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil or other PDE5 inhibitor

title: Anticoagulants, antiplatelets and NSAIDs
protocolCondition: Warfarin, and NSAIDs/aspirin / anticoagulants and antiplatelets
summary: Reject. Warfarin, NSAIDs, aspirin, antiplatelets — bleeding-risk consistency with S5.
source: EDM-PE-01 S7 — SSRIs increase bleeding risk with anticoagulants/NSAIDs; consistent with S5 bleeding decline
rationale: SSRIs, including dapoxetine, are recognised to increase bleeding risk in combination with anticoagulants and NSAIDs. Given this service already declines any history of bleeding or clotting problems (Section 5), disclosed warfarin or regular NSAID use is treated as a reject rather than a caution.

title: Low-dose aspirin
protocolRef: S7 — Warfarin, NSAIDs, aspirin (split pending Clinical Lead decision)
protocolCondition: Low-dose aspirin (split pending Clinical Lead decision)
summary: Reject (current policy). Low-dose aspirin tagged separately for possible future Clinical Lead change to counsel.
source: EDM-PE-01 S7 — S7 warfarin/NSAID/aspirin row — currently reject; may move to counsel later
rationale: Grouped with warfarin/NSAID/aspirin bleeding-risk reject for consistency with Section 5. Held as its own rule so Clinical Lead can switch outcome to counsel without losing SCR detection.

title: Prescribed sedatives and opioids
protocolRef: S8 Step 6 — sedatives (separated from recreational drugs)
protocolCondition: Prescribed sedatives / benzodiazepines (consultation medicines list)
summary: Reject. Prescribed sedatives/benzodiazepines on the Step 6 exclusion list.
source: EDM-PE-01 S8 Step 6 — Consultation Step 6 lists benzodiazepines with recreational drugs — separated in SCR library
rationale: Consultation Step 6 asks about recreational drugs including benzodiazepines. Prescribed sedatives are separated in the SCR keyword library but still block the remote pathway where they increase drowsiness/syncope risk alongside dapoxetine.
rejectIf: Benzodiazepine or prescribed sedative on SCR

title: Recreational and non-prescribed substances
protocolCondition: Recreational drugs (e.g. MDMA/ecstasy, amphetamines, LSD, other narcotics)
summary: Reject. Recreational drugs — SmPC advice; several carry serotonin syndrome risk.
source: EDM-PE-01 S7 / S8 Step 6 — SmPC (via ESNM40): do not combine dapoxetine with recreational drugs
rationale: Patients should be advised not to combine dapoxetine with recreational drugs. Several (MDMA, amphetamines) carry an additional specific serotonin syndrome risk.
rejectIf: Recreational drug use disclosed on SCR/history

title: Alcohol use
protocolCondition: Alcohol
summary: Counsel — do not combine dapoxetine with alcohol (dizziness, drowsiness, syncope risk).
source: EDM-PE-01 S7 — SmPC (via ESNM40): do not combine with alcohol — counselling point, not decline
rationale: Patients should be advised not to combine dapoxetine with alcohol, as both can cause drowsiness and additively increase the risk of dizziness or syncope. This service treats alcohol as a counselling point rather than an outright decline, consistent with the consultation script (warning, not a block) — but the warning must be given clearly.
counselText: You should not drink alcohol while taking dapoxetine (Priligy). Alcohol can increase side effects including dizziness, drowsiness, reduced alertness and fainting, and may increase the risk of accidental injury.

title: Finasteride 1 mg for hair loss — NOT an exclusion
matchRuleNames: Finasteride 1 mg for hair loss — NOT an exclusion
protocolCondition: Finasteride 1 mg for hair loss — NOT an exclusion
summary: Not an exclusion. Finasteride 1 mg (hair loss) does not itself contraindicate dapoxetine.
source: EDM-PE-01 S7 — S7 alpha-blocker row note — finasteride has no known direct interaction with dapoxetine
rationale: Finasteride, sometimes co-prescribed with tamsulosin for BPH, has no known direct interaction with dapoxetine itself. Finasteride 1 mg for hair loss is tagged none so it does not decline the PE pathway. (Finasteride 5 mg / dutasteride remain linked to prostate exclusion.)

title: Finasteride 5 mg and dutasteride
protocolCondition: Finasteride 5 mg / dutasteride (prostate signal)
summary: Reject. Finasteride 5 mg or dutasteride indicate prostate treatment — S5 prostate exclusion.
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 — S5 prostate problems — 5 mg finasteride/dutasteride corroborate prostate pathway
rationale: Captured by the prostate-problems exclusion in Section 5. Distinct from finasteride 1 mg hair-loss dosing which is not an exclusion.

title: Indicators of acquired premature ejaculation
protocolCondition: Indicators of acquired premature ejaculation (proposed)
summary: Flag. Markers of acquired PE — confirm diagnosis and exclude secondary causes.
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 — Proposed acquired-PE screening — flag for wider assessment
rationale: Acquired PE may be secondary to ED, GU infection, endocrine disease or medicines. Flag for prescriber review that licensed diagnostic criteria and Section 5 exclusions still hold before supply.
askPatient: Any new meds, GU symptoms, or ED?

title: Allergy to dapoxetine
protocolCondition: Allergic or hypersensitive to dapoxetine
summary: Reject. Allergy/hypersensitivity to dapoxetine (Priligy).
source: EDM-PE-01 S5 — Standard hypersensitivity contraindication
rationale: Universal contraindication for any medicine in a patient with known hypersensitivity to it.
